questions.q: Which plan best suits a 350–450 word narrative?
options: A war story across three countries
Two characters, one setting, one evening, one central problem
questions.why: Keep it small so the story is developed, not summarised.

questions.q: Which line of dialogue is punctuated correctly?
questions.why: Punctuation goes inside the speech marks, with a lower-case tag after a comma.

questions.q: Which sentence shows nervousness rather than telling it?
options: He felt extremely anxious and scared.
He was nervous because he was worried.
His fingers drummed on the table as the phone stayed silent.
questions.why: Showing uses action and detail so the reader infers the feeling.

questions.q: Give two ways to build tension in a narrative.
questions.model: Any two: short sentences or fragments at the crisis; slowing the pace with detail at key moments; delaying the answer; foreshadowing; focusing on small sensory details.
points: e.g. short sentences, pace, delay, foreshadowing, sensory detail
